description: A conversation attached to one request, shared by the requestor and everyone processing it. It is the only channel in the system: there is no email, so a reviewer who needs a clarification either returns the request or asks here. Mounted on the detail page, the edit page and all five review pages.

pages: mounted on every request page in IRMS-old

happy_path.result: the thread loads oldest-first under the request, with each author's name and role

happy_path.action: types a message and posts it
happy_path.result: it appears immediately, optimistically, and is confirmed when the mutation resolves
the body updates and an 'edited' marker appears
it is removed after a confirmation

alternate_paths.name: Someone else's message
alternate_paths.trigger: a participant presses edit or delete on a message they did not write
alternate_paths.result: the controls are not offered, and the procedures refuse with FORBIDDEN if called anyway

alternate_paths.name: ADD_COMMENT revoked
alternate_paths.result: the composer is disabled with a reason, and comment.create refuses

alternate_paths.name: No access to the request
alternate_paths.trigger: a USER who does not own the request
alternate_paths.result: comment.list refuses before any message is returned — the thread inherits the request's access rule exactly

alternate_paths.name: Post fails
alternate_paths.result: the optimistic message is marked failed with a retry, and nothing is silently lost

alternate_paths.name: Empty thread
alternate_paths.result: an empty state inviting the first message, not a blank panel

trpc_procedures.name: list
guards: the caller owns the request OR holds a staff role — the same rule as request.getById
trpc_procedures.description: Ordered oldest-first, each joined to its author's name and role.

trpc_procedures.name: create
trpc_procedures.description: userId comes from the session, never from input.

trpc_procedures.name: update
trpc_procedures.description: Only the author may edit. A director editing a requestor's words would make the thread worthless as a record.

trpc_procedures.name: delete
trpc_procedures.description: Hard delete. There is no moderation model and no soft-delete column.

components.name: RequestCommentThread
components.heroui_note: None. AppCommentSection supplies the composer, the optimistic post with retry, the edit and delete affordances, the 'edited' marker, relative timestamps and the empty state — all of which the old hand-rolled CommentThread implemented partially.
components.description: Maps RequestComment rows onto AppCommentSection's CommentItem shape: author is { id, name, handle: role label }, body is message, createdAt and editedAt from the row. onSubmit, onEdit and onDelete are the three mutations. Reactions and replies are NOT wired — the model has no parentId and no reaction table, so those props stay unset.

hooks.note: create, update and delete. Optimistic update on create, with rollback on failure.

functional: The thread is mounted on the request detail page, the edit page and all five review pages, with the same component and the same props everywhere.
Messages are ordered oldest-first — this is a conversation, not a feed.
Each message shows the author's name and their ROLE, because 'Carlos Santos' means nothing to a requestor and 'IDO Chairperson' does.
An edited message carries a visible marker and its updatedAt.
Delete asks for confirmation and then removes the row outright.
The composer is disabled with a stated reason when the caller lacks ADD_COMMENT.

Replies, reactions and mentions are deliberately not enabled — the data model has no parentId, no reaction table and no directory query, and half-wiring AppCommentSection's optional props would render controls that cannot work.
Message length is capped at 2000 characters, and the composer shows the remaining count as it approaches the cap.
authorization: Read access exactly mirrors request.getById: owner or staff role. The thread must never be more visible than the request it hangs on.
Posting additionally requires the ADD_COMMENT grant, which every role holds by default and an admin can revoke.
Editing and deleting are gated on AUTHORSHIP, not on role. No role, including DIRECTOR, may edit or delete another person's message.
userId on a new comment comes from the session; the input carries no author field.
ADMIN cannot read the thread, for the same reason they cannot read the request.
ux: The empty state invites the first message and says who can see it — 'Visible to you and everyone processing this request'.
An optimistic message shows as pending until confirmed, and as failed with a retry if the mutation rejects. A message that quietly disappears is the worst outcome here.
Timestamps are relative with the absolute value on hover.
The composer keeps its draft if the user navigates within the page; a lost half-written question is why people stop using the thread.
Edit and delete are shown only on the caller's own messages — the server refusal is the gate, but offering a control that always fails is a defect of its own.

rules.zod_rule: z.string().trim().min(1, 'Message is required').max(2000, 'Messages are limited to 2000 characters')

server_guards.guard: owner or staff role, then assertPermission(ADD_COMMENT)
server_guards.error: FORBIDDEN — Access denied / You don't have permission to perform this action
FORBIDDEN — Cannot edit another user's comment
FORBIDDEN — Cannot delete another user's comment

server_guards.guard: message is trimmed then length-checked server-side

covers: the request owner can list and post
an IDO_OFFICER can list and post on someone else's request
an unrelated USER cannot list — FORBIDDEN
a user without ADD_COMMENT cannot post but can still list
a DIRECTOR cannot edit a requestor's comment
a DIRECTOR cannot delete a requestor's comment
the author can edit and delete their own
userId is taken from the session even when the input carries another userId
a requestor posts and an IDO officer sees it on the review page
edit and delete controls appear only on the caller's own messages
a failed post shows as failed with a retry rather than disappearing
the empty state is shown on a request with no messages

acceptance_criteria.then: they render oldest-first, each with the author's name and role label

acceptance_criteria.given: a message written by the requestor
acceptance_criteria.then: no edit or delete control is shown on it, and a crafted comment.update for it returns FORBIDDEN

acceptance_criteria.given: a USER whose ADD_COMMENT grant was revoked
acceptance_criteria.then: they can read the thread and the composer is disabled with a stated reason

acceptance_criteria.when: they call comment.list for a request they do not own
acceptance_criteria.then: the call returns FORBIDDEN and no message body is returned
the body updates and an 'edited' marker appears with the new timestamp

edge_cases: The thread's read rule and the request's read rule are the same rule written twice; extract one shared helper, or a change to one leaves the other exposing messages about a request the caller cannot open.

Deleting a request cascades its comments (onDelete: Cascade), but nothing in the app deletes requests — if that ever changes, the cascade is already correct and must not be replaced with a manual sweep.
AppCommentSection's optional reaction and reply props must stay unset, not stubbed with no-ops; a reply control that posts a top-level comment is worse than no reply control.
Optimistic create must roll back on failure AND keep the typed text, or a network blip costs the user their message.
Message is a free-text column rendered as text, never as HTML — the composer must not gain rich text without an escaping decision.

A comment's author may later change role; the thread shows the CURRENT role from the join, which can read oddly on old messages. That is accepted — storing the role at write time is not worth the column.
out_of_scope: Threaded replies, reactions and @-mentions — the data model supports none of them.
Notifications or email on a new message — there is no notification system.
Attachments inside a comment — request attachments are the file channel.
Moderation, soft delete or an audit trail of edits — the thread is a conversation, not a record of record; AuditLog is that.
